solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scorn satisfied politician taking over from noon, later

indicators.note: taking over from someone means replacing them, so one letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: satisfied means content
MP is a Member of Parliament
N stands for noon; 'later' picks the second of the two Ns in the word

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied politician sneers at a rival by arriving after midday.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTENT has two Ns; 'later' tells you to swap the second one for MP, giving CONTEMPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is a direct synonym of scorn, the feeling that something is worthless.

clue.text: Men, hot rampant horny beasts

indicators.note: a rampant beast rears up on its hind legs, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

blocks.note: OR is 'other ranks', soldiers who are not officers
hot in the sense of sexually attractive

explanation.surface: A lurid line about lustful men and wild randy animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' looks like part of the smutty surface but means literally having horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Oryxes are long-horned African and Arabian antelopes, so they are beasts with horns.

clue.text: Fish starter for four

blocks.note: first meaning: a small brightly coloured tropical aquarium fish
second meaning: a prefix, a word's starter, meaning four

explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests a first course at a dinner for four people; here it is the beginning of a word, as in tetrahedron.
explanation.definitionFit: The tetra is a popular freshwater aquarium fish, and the Greek-derived prefix tetra- denotes the number four in compound words.

clue.text: Friend buried in another's plot

indicators.note: something buried in something else lies inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate
another word for a friend

explanation.surface: One friend is buried in another friend's grave plot.
explanation.walkthrough: China for friend is Cockney rhyming slang, from 'china plate' rhyming with mate; 'another's' reads as 'another is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to scheme or contrive secretly, the same as to plot as a verb.

clue.text: Dramatic scene in Arab country, disembodied limb at uprising

indicators.note: removing the body of a word leaves only its outside letters
something rising up in a down clue is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the United Arab Emirates
the first and last letters of limb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of an uprising in an Arab country, with a severed limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking group or picture, especially a staged one in a play, so a dramatic scene.

clue.text: Reject instrument, good for nothing

indicators.note: to reject something is to throw it back, so the words are turned around

blocks.note: the Indian stringed instrument
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Throw out an instrument that is good for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good for nothing' reads as one idiom, but it splits: good is wordplay and 'for nothing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge, given without payment.

clue.text: Judge with gold piercing backed product of Fabergé

indicators.note: something piercing another goes through it, so it ends up inside
backed means put into reverse, so the word reads the other way

blocks.note: Carl Fabergé was famed for his jewelled eggs
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An appraiser examines a gold-encrusted Fabergé treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To gauge is to estimate or assess, which is to judge as a verb.

clue.text: Going by hearsay, cane toad abandoned lake

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and uninhibited, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A rumour says a cane toad has been left behind by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on stories people tell rather than proof, which is relying on hearsay.

clue.text: Computer service hospital worker finds alien

blocks.note: a junior doctor in training
ET is the film extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A junior doctor discovers an extraterrestrial patient while fixing a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The internet is the global network that provides online services to computers.

clue.text: Spiritual girl reported to have convulsion

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: a girl is a miss, which is said the same as the start of the answer
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A religious girl is said to have had a fit, as in a tale of possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystic describes things relating to hidden spiritual truth or religious mystery.

clue.text: Not fair, monster gets over trap

indicators.note: one word getting over another covers it on both sides, so it wraps around it

blocks.note: a brute is a savage beast
a net is used to trap things

explanation.surface: It is unfair: the monster gets past the trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fair' sounds like a complaint of injustice; it means not fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette has dark brown hair, the opposite of a fair-haired blonde.

clue.text: Correspondent blue, vital errors penned in review

indicators.note: letters penned in are enclosed within the words that follow, written inside them
to review is to look back, so the hidden letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters running from the end of blue into the start of errors

explanation.surface: A journalist, feeling low, admits critical mistakes in a published critique.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is written backwards across blUE VITAL ERrors.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative and correspondent can both be adjectives meaning matching or in proportion to something else.

clue.text: One should respect these trees

blocks.note: first meaning: older people who are owed deference
second meaning: small trees bearing white flowers and dark berries

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as advice to respect nature; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Elders are senior people traditionally shown respect, and the elder is a shrub or tree of the genus Sambucus.

clue.text: Repeat working over two words initially changed from cut and paste

indicators.note: working means in operation or being worked on, so these letters are reshaped
two new words are made by altering only the first letter of the word that follows
one part laid over another covers it on both sides, wrapping around it

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
the first letter of cut is changed twice to make two new words

explanation.surface: It sounds like computer advice on repeating a cut-and-paste operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and paste' looks like the computing phrase, but 'paste' alone is the definition; the two altered words sit inside the shuffled letters of repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a spread made by grinding roasted peanuts into a thick paste.

clue.text: Showman with young faithful follower touring East

indicators.note: touring a place means going all around it, so one word encircles another

blocks.note: a pup is a young animal
Saint Peter, a disciple of Jesus
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A showman tours the East with a young devoted sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppeteer entertains audiences by working puppets, a kind of showman.

clue.text: Intended to chance red hot cooking

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: to bet is to take a chance
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone meant to risk something while the kitchen is red hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like a verb meaning planned, but it is the noun for a fiancé.
explanation.definitionFit: Your intended is the person you are engaged to marry, your betrothed.

clue.text: Amount of leaves outside company event creates problematic situation

indicators.note: something outside another surrounds it, so it wraps around the inner word

blocks.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
a company's Annual General Meeting

explanation.surface: Paperwork piled around a company meeting creates a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' suggests trees, but these are sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is literally a bog and figuratively a tricky predicament that is hard to escape.

clue.text: Extra agile of mind

blocks.note: supple means flexible and agile
mental means relating to the mind

explanation.surface: Someone extra quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplemental means added on as a supplement, so additional or extra.

clue.text: Old collector's item on empty bed gone forever

indicators.note: an empty word has had its middle removed, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: ex means former
a charity collector rattles a collecting tin
a cot is a bed; only its first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: An antique collectible on a stripped bed has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collector's item' suggests an antique; it is the tin a charity collector carries.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct species has died out completely and will never return.

clue.text: Man casually dropped before the Queen

blocks.note: fell means dropped down
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A man collapsed in front of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Feller is an informal spelling of fellow, a casual word for a man or chap.

clue.text: Vice admiral initially took to the front very well

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the first letter of admiral
greed is one of the seven deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: A vice admiral took his ship forward very successfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice admiral' reads as a naval rank, but splits into a sin and a letter; 'took to the front' puts the letter before the sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'agreed' or 'very well' both signal consent to a proposal.

clue.text: Evildoer has distinctive way of doing things in lair

indicators.note: in places one item within another, enclosed by it

blocks.note: a den is an animal's lair
MO is modus operandi, a characteristic method

explanation.surface: A villain has a trademark method inside a hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit, figuratively a wicked person who does harm.

clue.text: Junk hotels do hammer home, perhaps

indicators.note: junk is scrap and rubbish, so these letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Run-down hotels really push a point home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer home' looks like the phrase meaning to stress a point; it means the home of a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool shed is where a hammer and other tools are kept, so a hammer's house, as one example.

clue.text: Bolt, in brief, Olympic medallist

blocks.note: Steve Cram, British 1500m silver medallist in 1984, with his first name cut to an initial

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, summed up as an Olympic champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt suggests the Jamaican sprinter, but here it is a verb; 'in brief' tells you to shorten Steve to S.
explanation.definitionFit: To scram is to run off quickly, which is to bolt.

clue.text: Recalling duck names confused park official

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the word is taken backwards
confused letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A muddled park keeper tries to remember the names of the ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park' suggests a public garden, but here it is a football park, a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A linesman is an assistant referee who runs the touchline at a football ground.

clue.text: Announcer drove around US city, heading west

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word surrounds the other
west is leftwards in an across clue, so the word reads from right to left

blocks.note: to drove animals is to herd them
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A broadcaster drove round an American city before setting off west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' looks like the past of drive, but it is a verb meaning to move livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an official messenger who made proclamations, so an announcer.

clue.text: The suspect fled capital city

indicators.note: suspect means dubious and not right, so these letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
fled means ran away

explanation.surface: The suspect escaped from the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital of Iran.

clue.text: Ship on ocean with computers returning line revealed through water

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are taken backwards
in an across clue one thing placed on another comes after it, so the ship is sent second

blocks.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
IT is information technology
Noah's Ark

explanation.surface: A computer-equipped ship at sea leaves a line seen through the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'ship on' the rest puts the ship last.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line left on a shore, or round a bath, showing how high the water reached.
